words.gloss: embryo (garbha); to be attended to, care

hindi: अब इसके बाद हम गर्भोपचरणीय नामक शारीर की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall expound the Śārīra (on the body) named Garbhopacaraṇīya (the care to be given to the embryo).
notes: Opening formula of a chapter. 'garbhopacaraṇīya' is taken as the chapter name (literally 'what is to be attended to regarding the embryo'); 'śārīra' is the section on the body.

hindi: पहले मास में गर्भिणी संस्कार किया हुआ दूध, मात्रा के अनुसार ठण्डा, समय पर पिए।
english: In the first month the pregnant woman should drink milk that has been prepared, cool, in measure, at the time.
notes: 'prathamemāsi' is two words printed together (e + m, no sandhi), not an error. The nature of the preparation (upasaṃskṛta) is not stated. 'kāle' is taken as 'at the time' (the due time); the text does not say which time.

words.gloss: śāliparṇī (Desmodium gangeticum; standard); palāśa (Butea monosperma; probable)
gold; silver; boiled; cool; water; after-drink

hindi: उस में भी पहली बारह रातों तक दूध से उत्पन्न घी, शालिपर्णी और पलाश के साथ उबाला हुआ, सोने और चाँदी के साथ उबाले हुए ठण्डे जल के अनुपान सहित, पिए।
english: In that (month) also, for the first twelve nights, she should drink ghee (sarpis) arising from milk, boiled with śāliparṇī (Desmodium gangeticum) and palāśa (probably Butea monosperma), having as after-drink (anupāna) cool water boiled with gold and silver.
notes: 'tasmin' is taken as 'in that (month)'. 'ādyam dvādaśarātram' is taken as accusative of duration: 'for the first twelve nights'. Identifications: śāliparṇī = Desmodium gangeticum (standard); palāśa = Butea monosperma (probable; palāśa can also simply mean 'leaf', in which case 'with the leaves of śāliparṇī' is possible). 'kṣīrodbhava' ghee = ghee arising from milk. The bahuvrīhi 'kanaka...anupānam' qualifies the ghee: 'having as anupāna cool water boiled with gold and silver'.

hindi: मीठे और ठण्डे, अधिकतर तरल और अनुकूल से सायं और प्रातः आहार कराए।
english: One should have her take food of sweet and cool (ones), mostly liquid and suitable (sātmya), in the evening and in the morning.

text_flags.why: possible: 'khādu' is not a word; svādu 'sweet' fits the sense (milk, ghee and cooling regimen) and kh/sv is a likely scan or typing confusion.

notes: Elliptical: the nouns for the 'sweet and cool, mostly liquid, suitable' items are not stated, so '(ones)' is used. The case of the adjectives is read as instrumental/accusative of the food; the subject of āhārayet is not stated. sātmya = what is agreeable/habitually suited to her (not further defined here).

hindi: और अभ्यंग तथा उद्वर्तन का सेवन न करे।
english: And she should not resort to oil massage (abhyaṅga) or rubbing with powders (udvartana).
notes: The subject (the pregnant woman) is understood from unit 2.

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर, कहे अनुसार दोष करने वालों को पाँचवें मास तक त्याग दे।
english: On a conjectural reading, she should avoid, up to the fifth month, the doṣa-causing (ones) as stated.

text_flags.why: possible: 'ārpacamān' is not a word; the shape of the letters fits 'āpañcamāt' (ā + pañcama, 'up to the fifth'), but this is only a guess and the sense of a time limit is the only firm part.

notes: Damaged or unclear print: 'ārpacamān' is kept unsplit and unglossed; the translation 'up to the fifth month' is a conjecture only. 'ā + ablative' would mean 'up to'. 'doṣakara' is taken as 'causing doṣa (disturbance of the humours)'; 'yathokta' refers back to something said earlier, not in this chunk. The subject (the pregnant woman) is understood.

hindi: विशेष रूप से दूसरे में मधुर औषधों से पकाया हुआ दूध पिए।
english: Especially in the second (month), she should drink milk cooked with sweet medicines (madhura-auṣadha).
notes: 'dvitīye' is taken as 'in the second (month)', month understood from unit 2. 'madhura-auṣadha' is literally 'sweet medicines'; the text does not list them here and none is identified.

hindi: तीसरे में वही, घी और मधु के साथ।
english: In the third (month), that same (milk), with ghee and honey.
notes: Elliptical: the verb (pibet, 'should drink') is carried from the previous unit and no verb is supplied in the translation. 'tadeva' refers to the milk of the previous unit; 'sarpirmadhubhyām' = with ghee (sarpis) and honey (madhu), instrumental dual.

words.gloss: akṣa (a measure); measure; fresh butter (navanīta); joined with

hindi: चौथे में अक्ष मात्रा के नवनीत से युक्त।
english: In the fourth (month), joined with fresh butter (navanīta) in the measure of an akṣa.
notes: Elliptical: verb and the substance (the milk of 7/8) are carried over; none is supplied. The avagraha in 'caturthe'kṣa' is printed correctly. akṣa is a measure of weight (a synonym of karṣa, glossary).

hindi: पाँचवें में क्षीरसर्पिस् यानी दूध का घी।
english: In the fifth (month), milk-ghee (kṣīrasarpis), ghee of milk.
notes: Elliptical: the verb is carried over. The compound could also be read as a dvandva 'milk and ghee'; the plainer reading 'ghee of milk' is taken (compare 'kṣīrodbhavaṃ sarpiḥ' in unit 3).

hindi: छठे में वही, मधुर औषधों से पकाया हुआ।
english: In the sixth (month), that same, cooked with sweet medicines (madhura-auṣadha).
notes: Elliptical: verb carried over. It is not stated whether 'tadeva' refers to the milk-ghee of unit 10 or the milk of unit 7; the translation keeps it open.

hindi: और सातवें में।
english: And in the seventh (month).
notes: Incomplete as printed: no substance or verb is given for the seventh month. GROUPING: this unit appears to continue into the next unit or to have lost its content; nothing is supplied here.

hindi: और उस में गर्भ के केशों की उत्पत्ति से माता को विदाह यानी जलन होती है, ऐसा स्त्रियाँ कहती हैं; ऐसा नहीं, भगवान् आत्रेय।
english: And in that (month), 'burning (vidāha) of the mother occurs through the arising of the embryo's hair,' so women say; 'not so,' (says) the venerable Ātreya.
notes: 'tasmin' is taken as 'in that (month)', the seventh of unit 12. The verb of speaking for Ātreya is not stated (carried from 'bhāṣante'); 'says' is supplied in English in brackets only for readability. vidāha = burning (probably a burning sensation, heartburn-like); the text gives no further definition.

words.gloss: itching; kikisa (probably stretch marks of pregnancy; probable)

hindi: गर्भ के दबाव से तो दोष हृदय तक पहुँचकर जलाते हैं; तब खुजली उत्पन्न होती है, खुजली वाला किकिस, सम्भवतः गर्भावस्था की धारियाँ।
english: But from the pressure of the embryo, the doṣas, having reached the heart (hṛdaya), burn; then itching arises, (and) kaṇḍūkikisa (itching with kikisa, probably the stretch marks of pregnancy).
notes: Last token 'kaṇḍūkikisaṃ': probably kaṇḍū + kikisa (kikkisa), a skin condition of pregnancy, identified as stretch marks (striae) - probable only. The repetition of kaṇḍū after 'kaṇḍūr jāyate' is odd; the reading as a compound 'itching-kikisa' with jāyate carried is tentative. The line seems to end without a verb. 'doṣāḥ' = the doṣas (doctrinal term, kept).

hindi: वहाँ कोल यानी सम्भवतः बेर के जल के साथ, मधुर औषधों से पकाए हुए नवनीत का हथेली भर इस स्त्री को दे।
english: In that case, with water of kola (probably jujube), one should give her a palm's measure of fresh butter (navanīta) cooked with sweet medicines.

text_flags.why: possible: ḍ for d is a common print confusion; 'kola-udaka' (jujube water) gives sense and the metre of a prose line is no evidence.

notes: kola = jujube (Ziziphus jujuba), probable; kola can also mean other things (disputed), so the identity is hedged. 'koloḍaka' read as kola-udaka 'kola water' on the corrected reading; if 'koloḍaka' were a word, it is unknown. 'asyai' = to her, the pregnant woman.

words.gloss: sandalwood (candana; Santalum album, standard); lotus stalk (mṛṇāla; standard); pastes
words.gram: m. inst. pl., dvandva then tat-puruṣa

hindi: और चन्दन यानी श्वेत चन्दन तथा मृणाल यानी कमलनाल के कल्कों से स्तन और पेट को मसले।
english: And with pastes (kalka) of candana (sandalwood) and mṛṇāla (lotus stalk), she should rub the breast and belly.

text_flags.why: possible: 'mṛdgīyāt' is not a form; the optative of √mṛd (kryādi) is mṛdnīyāt, and g for n is a likely print confusion.

notes: Subject: it is not stated who rubs; the pregnant woman is understood. 'stanodaram' is a singular dvandva, 'breast(s) and belly'. Identification: candana = Santalum album (standard); mṛṇāla = lotus stalk (Nelumbo nucifera, standard).

words.gloss: śirīṣa (Albizia lebbeck; standard); dhātakī (Woodfordia fruticosa; conjectural reading); mustard (sarṣapa); madhuka (probably licorice); powders
words.gram: m. inst. pl., dvandva then tat-puruṣa

hindi: अथवा शिरीष यानी सिरिस, अनुमानित पाठ पर धातकी यानी धाय के फूल, सरसों और मधुक यानी सम्भवतः मुलेठी के चूर्णों से।
english: Or with powders (cūrṇa) of śirīṣa (Albizia lebbeck), dhātakī (Woodfordia fruticosa, on a conjectural reading), mustard (sarṣapa) and madhuka (probably licorice).

text_flags.why: possible: 'ghātukī' is not a known drug name; dhātakī (Woodfordia fruticosa) is a common ingredient and gh/dh confusion is likely.

notes: Elliptical: the verb 'should rub' is carried from the previous unit. madhuka = licorice (Glycyrrhiza glabra), probable; mahua (Madhuca longifolia) is the other possibility. sarṣapa = mustard (Brassica species), standard. Hindi 'धातकी यानी धाय के फूल' rests on the conjecture.

words.gloss: kuṭaja (Holarrhena antidysenterica; standard); arjaka (a basil, probable); seed; mustā (Cyperus rotundus; standard); haridrā (turmeric, Curcuma longa; standard); pastes
nimba (Azadirachta indica; standard); kola (jujube, probable); surasā (holy basil, probable); mañjiṣṭhā (Rubia cordifolia; standard); pastes

hindi: अथवा कुटज यानी कुड़ा और अर्जक यानी सम्भवतः एक तुलसी के बीज, मुस्ता यानी नागरमोथा और हरिद्रा यानी हल्दी के कल्कों से; अथवा निम्ब यानी नीम, कोल यानी सम्भवतः बेर, सुरसा यानी सम्भवतः तुलसी और मञ्जिष्ठा यानी मजीठ के कल्कों से।
english: Or with pastes (kalka) of the seeds of kuṭaja (Holarrhena antidysenterica) and arjaka (probably a basil), mustā (nut grass, Cyperus rotundus) and haridrā (turmeric); or with pastes of nimba (neem), kola (probably jujube), surasā (probably holy basil) and mañjiṣṭhā (Indian madder).
notes: Elliptical: verb carried from unit 16. 'ḻ' in 'koḻa' is normalised to l (print habit, glossary). Whether 'bīja' governs both kuṭaja and arjaka is taken as yes (plural 'seeds of kuṭaja and arjaka'). 'surasa' read as surasā (holy basil); alternative readings (sura + sa..) not adopted. kola identity probable (jujube). arjaka = a white basil, probable. Hindi for kuṭaja is left as कुटज.

words.gloss: hare (śaśa); deer (hariṇa); punarnavā (Boerhavia diffusa; standard); mālatī (a jasmine, probably Jasminum grandiflorum; disputed); madhuka (probably licorice); cooked
words.gram: dvandva then tat-puruṣa, m. inst. sg.

words.gloss: karavīra (Nerium oleander; standard); leaf; paste; cooked

hindi: शश यानी खरगोश, हरिण यानी हिरन, पुनर्नवा यानी गदहपूर्णा, मालती और मधुक यानी सम्भवतः मुलेठी के साथ पकाए हुए जल से, पृषत यानी चित्तीदार हिरन के रुधिर से युक्त त्रिफला से, और करवीर के पत्तों के कल्क से पकाए हुए तेल से अभ्यंग।
english: Oil massage (abhyaṅga) with water cooked with hare (śaśa), deer (hariṇa), punarnavā (Boerhavia diffusa), mālatī (a jasmine, identity disputed) and madhuka (probably licorice); with triphalā (the three fruits) mixed with the blood of the spotted deer (pṛṣata); and with oil cooked with a paste of karavīra leaves (oleander).

text_flags.why: possible: 'siddhaināṃbhasā' is not a regular sandhi of siddhena + ambhasā (which gives siddhenāmbhasā); ai for e is a likely print error.

notes: The parts of hare and deer used are not stated (flesh is likely but not said). The text lists the water and the mixed triphalā and the oil as three instruments of one abhyaṅga; how they combine is not stated. pṛṣata = spotted deer. karavīra = Nerium oleander (standard); taila = oil (kind not stated). triphalā = harītakī, bibhītaka, āmalakī (standard). mālatī disputed.

words.gram: m. inst. sg., dvandva then tat-puruṣa

hindi: फिर मालती और मधुक के साथ पकाए हुए जल से पारिषेक यानी सींचना।
english: Pouring (pariṣeka) again with water cooked with mālatī and madhuka.
notes: Elliptical (no verb). 'punar' is taken as 'again'; it could also mean 'and further'. For mālatī and madhuka see unit 19.

hindi: खुजलाना त्याग दे।
english: She should avoid scratching.
notes: Subject understood (the pregnant woman).

words.gloss: disfigurement; avoidance; for the purpose of

hindi: त्वचा के फटने पर कुरूपता को दूर करने के लिए स्नान, उद्वर्तन और चन्दन का सेवन करे।
english: When the skin splits, for the purpose of avoiding disfigurement, she should make use of bathing, rubbing with powders (udvartana) and sandalwood (candana).
notes: The text has 'arthaṃsnāna' printed without a space; it is two words, not an error that changes the sense. 'tvagbheda' = splitting of the skin (probably the stretch marks of the previous units; the text does not say). 'ca' and 'śīlayet' are printed together as 'caśīlayet'.

hindi: और मीठा आहार, थोड़ा, थोड़े स्नेह यानी तेल या वसा और नमक वाला, थोड़े जल के अनुपान सहित खाए।
english: And she should eat sweet food, little in quantity, with little oil or fat (sneha) and salt, with little water as after-drink (anupāna).
notes: 'madhuram āhāram': sweet food (taste madhura). 'alpa' is taken as quantity, 'little'. Subject understood.

hindi: आठवें में घी वाली दूध की यवागू पिए।
english: In the eighth (month) she should drink milk gruel (yavāgū) containing ghee.
notes: 'aṣṭame' is taken as 'in the eighth (month)'. kṣīrayavāgū is a gruel made with milk (the compound could also be 'gruel and milk', not adopted).

hindi: ऐसा नहीं, षण्ढकाथो अस्पष्ट, अनुमानित पाठ पर, गर्भ को पिंगलता की बाधा के भय से।
english: 'Not so,' on a conjectural reading, says ṣaṇḍhakātho (unclear), from fear of the affliction of tawny colour to the embryo.

text_flags.why: possible: the printed word does not parse; it may hide a speaker's name (compare 'bhagavān ātreyaḥ' in unit 13) or a form of 'kath'; no firm reading.

notes: Damaged or unparsable print: 'ṣaṃḍhakātho' is kept unsplit; the speaker is probably an objecting teacher but this is conjectural. paiṅgalya = tawny, yellowish-brown colour (of what is not stated; the embryo's coloration is the likely sense). The objection is to the gruel of the previous unit. GROUPING: this unit appears to continue the discussion of unit 24 and to continue in unit 26.

hindi: पिंगलता की बाधा है, फिर भी ऐसा ही करे।
english: There is the affliction of tawny colour; even so, one should act thus.
notes: 'evam' points to the regimen of unit 24 (gruel with ghee), per context; this is not stated.

words.gloss: strength; complexion; sattva (mind, vitality); firm build; excellence; endowed with

hindi: वह रोग से रहित, बल, वर्ण, सत्त्व और संहनन की सम्पदा से युक्त, जातिजनों में अग्रगण्य सन्तान को जन्म देती है, ऐसा भगवान् आत्रेय कहते हैं।
english: She brings forth a child free of disease, endowed with the excellence of strength, complexion, sattva and body-build (saṃhanana), reckoned foremost among his kinsmen: so (says) the venerable Ātreya.
notes: The subject of 'janayati' is not stated; the woman who follows the regimen above is understood. 'saṃhanana' = firm, compact build of the body. 'sattva' is kept as a doctrinal term (mind, mental strength). 'jñātīnām agragaṇyam' = counted first among his relatives.

words.gloss: palala (probably sesame paste; disputed); milk; curd; whey (mastu); oil; salt; fruit; ghee; honey; joined with
words.gram: dvandva then tat-puruṣa, n. inst. sg.

hindi: बदर के जल से, जो पलल, दूध, दही, मस्तु, तेल, नमक, फल, घी और मधु से युक्त हो, आस्थापन यानी काढ़े की वस्ति दे।
english: One should administer an āsthāpana (decoction enema) with jujube (badara) water joined with palala (probably sesame paste), milk, curd, whey (mastu), oil, salt, fruit, ghee and honey.

text_flags.why: possible: 'gṛta' is not a word; ghṛta (ghee) fits the list of substances.

notes: palala is disputed: sesame paste (tila-kalka) is likely here, but 'flesh' is another meaning. 'phala' (fruit) is not specified. mastu = whey of curd. The object (the pregnant woman) is understood; the enema is described as in the previous units.

words.gloss: old; stool; cleansing; for the purpose of
madhuka (probably licorice); beginning with; sweet; medicines; cooked
words.gram: bahuvrīhi then tat-puruṣa, m. inst. sg.

words.gloss: for moving downward, for setting in order

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर पुराने मल की शुद्धि के लिए, और मधुक आदि मधुर औषधों से पकाए तेल से अनुवासन दे, वायु के अनुलोमन के लिए।
english: On a conjectural reading, for clearing the old stool, and with oil cooked with sweet medicines beginning with madhuka (probably licorice), one should administer an anuvāsana (oil enema), for the downward movement (anulomana) of the wind (vāyu).

text_flags.why: possible: 'vidviśśutti-' is not a word; viḍ-viśuddhi 'cleansing of stool' fits (d for ḍ, śś for ś, t for ddh), but the whole reading is conjectural.

notes: The first token is badly printed; the reading 'purāṇaviḍviśuddhyartham' (for cleansing of old stool) is a conjecture. 'madhukādi' = madhuka (probably licorice) and the others of the sweet group. anulomana = making move in the proper (downward) direction. vāyu = wind, here the Vāta in the body. Subject (the physician) understood.

hindi: क्योंकि वायु के अनुलोम होने पर वह सुख से, उपद्रव से रहित, प्रसव करती है।
english: For when the wind is moving downward, she gives birth easily, free of complications (upadrava).
notes: 'himārute' is two words printed together, 'hi mārute'. Subject (the woman) understood. 'upadrava' = complication.

hindi: गर्भिणी को तो झुकी हुई स्थिति में आस्थापन दे अथवा अनुवासन दे।
english: But to the pregnant woman, bent over (nyubja), one should administer either an āsthāpana (decoction enema) or an anuvāsana (oil enema).
notes: 'nyubja' is taken as 'bent over / face downward'; the exact posture is not described in the text. Sentence is the continuation of the instructions of 28-29.

words.gloss: opened; passage; because of the state

hindi: उस प्रकार उसके मार्ग के खुले होने से औषध ठीक से भीतर प्रवेश करता है।
english: In that way, because of the openness of her passage, the medicine (auṣadha) enters properly.

text_flags.why: possible: the genitive 'asyāḥ' is meant; the final visarga is lost in print (an instrumental 'asyā' with vivṛtamārgatayā would not fit).

notes: Printed 'tathā 'syā': tathā + asyāḥ (avagraha for the dropped a). The word 'mārga' (passage) is not further defined (compare 'garbhamārga' in unit 34). 'vivṛta' = opened.

hindi: इसके बाद प्रसव के समय तक चिकनी यवागुओं और जाङ्गल जीवों के रसों से उपचार करे, ऐसा भगवान् धन्वन्तरि कहते हैं।
english: After this, until the time of delivery, one should treat (her) with unctuous gruels (yavāgū) and with the juices (broths) of jāṅgala (dry-land) animals: so (says) the venerable Dhanvantari.
notes: 'jāṅgalarasa' = broth of animals of the dry-land (jāṅgala) class; the text does not name them. The object (the pregnant woman) is understood. 'ataḥ ūrdhvam' printed 'ataūrdhvaṃ'. The verb of speaking for Dhanvantari is not stated.

words.gloss: embryo; passage; receptacle (āśaya, probably the uterus)

hindi: नवें में तो उसी अनुवासन के तेल से पिचु योनि में रखे, गर्भ के मार्ग और आशय को स्नेहन के लिए।
english: In the ninth (month), however, from that same anuvāsana oil, a picu (cotton swab) should be inserted into the yoni (vagina), for the oiling of the passage of the embryo and the receptacle (āśaya).

text_flags.why: possible: 'snehanātham' is not a word and has no sense here; 'snehanārtham' (for oiling) fits, the r dropped in print.

notes: 'garbhamārgāśayayoḥ' can be read 'of the embryo's passage and receptacle' (taken) or 'of the garbha-mārga and the āśaya'; āśaya is probably the uterus (probable). picu = cotton swab (it is also a weight measure; here the object inserted). yoni here = the vaginal passage (it may mean womb elsewhere). The oil is the one used for anuvāsana in 29.

hindi: इससे पहले मास से आरम्भ करके क्रम से गर्भिणी के प्रसव के समय गर्भ को धारण करने वाली कुक्षि, कटि, पार्श्व और पीठ मृदु हो जाती है।
english: By this, beginning from the first month, step by step, at the time of delivery the belly (kukṣi) that bears the embryo, the waist (kaṭī), the flank (pārśva) and the back (pṛṣṭha) of the pregnant woman become soft.
notes: 'anena' refers to the regimen of the preceding units (not stated). 'garbhadhāriṇī' is taken as qualifying kukṣi ('the embryo-bearing belly'); it could also be a separate item (the embryo-bearing organ); the plainer reading is taken. The dvandva is a collective singular.

words.gloss: moving downward, in the proper direction

hindi: और वायु अनुलोम हो जाता है।
english: And the wind (vāyu) becomes anuloma (moving in the proper, downward direction).
notes: vāyu here = the Vāta in the body (doctrinal term).

hindi: और मूत्र तथा मल प्रकृतिस्थ हो जाते हैं और जरायु यानी गर्भ की झिल्ली और अपरा मार्ग को प्राप्त होता है।
english: And urine and stool become natural, and the jarāyu (afterbirth: placenta with membranes) goes to the passage.

text_flags.why: possible: the final anusvāra is dropped in print; the accusative is required by 'pratipadyate'.

notes: 'prakṛtibhūta' = become normal, as natural. jarāyu = foetal membranes / afterbirth (standard); the text does not say whether it comes out. 'mārga' = passage (not defined).

hindi: और वह बलवती समय पर सुख से इष्ट, स्वस्थ, दीर्घायु और सुखी पुत्र को जन्म देती है।
english: And the strong woman gives birth at the time, easily, to a desired son, healthy, long-lived and happy.
notes: 'putram' = son (not 'child'). 'kalya' = healthy. 'balavatī' is read as 'strong (woman)', subject. The 'at the time' (kāle) is the due time of delivery.

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर, बिल्व यानी बेल, कार्पासी यानी कपास, फंफेणा अस्पष्ट, पाटली, पिचुमन्द यानी नीम, अग्निमन्थ, मांसी यानी जटामांसी, वर्धमानक और पत्र भंग के काढ़े से, ठण्डे काढ़े से अथवा सब गन्ध वाले द्रव्यों के जल से गर्भिणी के लिए प्रतिदिन स्नान का उपदेश करे।
english: On a conjectural reading, one should prescribe daily bathing for the pregnant woman with a cooled decoction (kvātha) of bilva (bael), kārpāsī (cotton), phaṃpheṇā (unclear), pāṭalī (Stereospermum suaveolens), picumanda (neem), agnimantha (probably Premna), māṃsī (probably spikenard), vardhamānaka (identity disputed) and patrabhaṅga (unclear), or with water of all fragrant substances (sarvagandha).
notes: Damaged or unclear print in the long compound: 'phaṃpheṇā' is kept unsplit and unidentified; 'patrabhaṅga' (patra + bhaṅga) is unclear (it may be 'leaves, broken', or bhaṅgā = hemp; no firm reading). The rest of the compound is read as a list of plants (dvandva): bael, cotton, pāṭalī, neem, etc. 'garbhiṇyāḥ' is taken as dative-sense genitive 'for the pregnant woman'. 'sarvagandhodaka' = water prepared with all fragrant substances. The decoction is cool (śīta).

words.gram: n. loc. sg., bahuvrīhi (agrees with deśe)

hindi: और उसके नवें मास से पहले ही, अनुमानित पाठ पर हड्डी, कंकड़ और ठीकरों से रहित प्रशस्त स्थान में, वास्तुविद्या से प्रशस्त, सब ऋतुओं में सुखद, सब उपकरणों से युक्त, जिसमें अग्नि पास हो, पूर्व द्वार वाला अथवा उत्तर द्वार वाला सूतिकागार बनवाए।
english: And even before her ninth month, on a conjectural reading, one should have a delivery chamber (sūtikāgāra) made in an auspicious place free of bones, gravel and potsherds, approved by the science of building sites (vāstu-vidyā), comfortable in all seasons, furnished with all equipment, with fire kept at hand, with a door to the east or to the north.

text_flags.why: possible: genitive 'asyāḥ' with the visarga lost in print (as in unit 32).
possible: 'apṛtatā' is not a word; 'apahṛta' (removed) before asthi-śarkarā-kapāla fits, but the reading is conjectural.
possible: 'upṛtat' is not a word; 'upahṛta' (brought) fits 'sarvopakaraṇa', conjectural.

notes: Damaged print: 'apṛtatā' and 'upṛtat' are kept unsplit with gloss unclear; the translation 'free of bones, gravel and potsherds' and 'furnished with all equipment' follows the conjectural readings apahṛta and upahṛta and is hedged. 'vāstu-vidyā' = the science of sites and buildings. The two doors (east or north) are as printed. 'sūtikāgāra' = delivery chamber.

words.gram: pres. part. mid. ā-√vṛt, f. nom. sg.

words.gloss: made to move properly; wind; urine; stool

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर, वहाँ नक्षत्र आदि अनुकूल होने पर पुण्याह शब्द के साथ, गाय, ब्राह्मण और वृद्धों की ओर प्रदक्षिणा करती हुई प्रवेश करके, बहुत बार प्रसव कर चुकी, अनुक्ताभिः और अविपादाभिः अस्पष्ट, क्लेश सहने वाली स्त्रियों से घिरी हुई, स्वस्त्ययन में लगी हुई, अनुलोमन करने वाले आहार और विहार से वात, मूत्र और मल को अनुलोम की हुई प्रसव के समय की प्रतीक्षा करे।
english: On a conjectural reading: there, when the stars and the rest are favourable, with the utterance of puṇyāha (auspicious-day formula), but circling clockwise round the cows, brahmins and elders, having entered, surrounded by women who have given birth many times, anuktābhiḥ and avipādābhiḥ (unclear), able to bear hardship, devoted to auspicious rites (svastyayana), with wind, urine and stool made to move properly by regulating food and conduct, she should await the time of delivery.

text_flags.why: possible: tu + ā gives 'tvā'; the doubled avagraha mark is a print habit; the sense 'circling round' is not firm.
possible: tr for vr is a common OCR confusion; 'surrounded' fits.
possible: 'nerā' for 'nair ā' (ai printed e), and 'mtra' for 'mūtra' (ū lost); the sense fits.

notes: Damaged or unclear print: 'anuktābhiḥ' and 'avipādābhiḥ' are real forms but the sense in a list of qualities of attendants is unclear (they may hide other words); they are kept unglossed. 'prasūtābhir bahuśaḥ' is read as 'by those who have given birth many times'. 'tu' with 'āvartamānā' is awkward and uncertain. The ritual 'puṇyāha' is an auspicious-day benediction. 'pradakṣiṇam' = keeping the right side toward the object. Subject (the woman) is understood; the sentence is long and the join with unit 40 (the chamber) is by context.

hindi: और मल तथा मूत्र की थोड़ी सी भी रुकावट में फलवर्तियाँ यानी बत्तियाँ रखे।
english: And even in a slight obstruction (vibandha) of stool and urine, one should insert phalavartis (suppositories).
notes: 'svalpe'pi' is su-alpe api, 'even slight'. 'phalavarti' = a suppository (varti = wick-like roll); the substance 'phala' is not specified here. The text speaks of obstruction of stool and urine (vibandha = constipation / retention). Insertion site and subject are not stated.

words.gram: n. nom. sg., dvandva then tat-puruṣa

hindi: तब जिसका प्रसव निकट है, उसमें थकावट, ग्लानि, मानो बन्धन छूटे हुए दोनों नेत्र, थूक, मूत्र और मल की अधिकता, कुक्षि की शिथिलता, नीचे भारीपन, अन्न में अरुचि, पेट, हृदय, कटि, बस्ति और वंक्षण में पीड़ा; चुभन, फटन, शूल, फड़कन और योनि के स्राव होते हैं।
english: Then, in her whose delivery is near, there occur exhaustion (klama), weariness (glāni), the two eyes as if with released fastenings, abundance of spitting, urine and stool, looseness of the belly, heaviness below, lack of desire for food, pain (vedanā) in the belly (udara), heart (hṛdaya), waist, bladder (basti) and groin; and pricking (toda), tearing (bheda), pain (śūla), throbbing (sphuraṇa) and flows (sravaṇa) of the yoni occur.

text_flags.why: possible: a stray 't' in 'darathṛdaya'; 'udara-hṛdaya' fits.

notes: Complex list; the grammar of 'vedanā ... udarahṛdaya...' is not certain (it could be pain located in these parts followed by the list toda... as its kinds). 'stravaṇa' (st for sr) is read sravaṇa, flow. 'niṣṭīvikā' = spitting (or excess saliva). 'mukta-bandhane iva akṣiṇī' = the eyes as if with loosened bonds. 'basti' here = bladder; hṛdaya = heart (standard). 'yonyāḥ ... sravaṇāni' read as flows of the yoni (vagina); alternative: 'yonyā bhavanti' is correct sandhi of yonyāḥ + bhavanti; 'yonyā' as an instrumental is not adopted.

hindi: उसके बाद आवियों यानी प्रसव की पीड़ाओं का प्रकट होना और गर्भ के जल का बहना।
english: After that, the appearance of the āvīs (labour pains) and the flow of the water of the embryo (garbhodaka: amniotic fluid).
notes: āvī = labour pains (probable); garbhodaka = amniotic fluid (probable). No verb in the Sanskrit; none supplied.

hindi: तब उसे, जिसके गर्भ का समय उपस्थित हो, जिसने कौतुक और मंगल किया हो, हाथ में पुंनाम नामक फल लिए हो, भली-भाँति तेल लगी हो, गर्म जल से सींची गई हो, घी सहित यवागू पिलाए।
english: Then one should make her drink gruel (yavāgū) with ghee, her to whom the embryo has come forward, who has performed the kautuka and auspicious rites, with a fruit called punnāma (unidentified) in her hand, well anointed with oil and sprinkled with hot water.
notes: 'puṃnāmaphala' = fruit of a masculine name (unidentified); the text does not name the fruit. 'upasthitagarbhā' is literally 'with the embryo arrived/present', i.e. delivery at hand (interpretation not in the text). 'kautuka' = a ritual for protection or auspiciousness; 'svabhyaktā' = well anointed with oil (the oil is not named). 'punnāma' printed with geminate n for puṃ-nāma.

words.gloss: very; red; of a bull; hide; covering

words.gram: pres. part. mid. √śī, f. acc. sg.
pres. part. caus. ā-√śvas, f. nom. pl.

hindi: तब अच्छे लाल बैल के चमड़े के आच्छादन वाली कोमल भूमि की शय्या पर लेटी हुई, उत्तान, जंघाओं और पीठ को मोड़े हुए सूतिका को, नए वस्त्र पहने, सन्देह से परे, देखने में प्रिय, प्रौढ़ आयु की, प्रसव में कुशल, निर्भीक, कटे नखों वाली स्त्रियाँ मधुर और सत्य वाणियों से आश्वासन देती हुई घेरकर सेवा करें।
english: Then women with new (unworn) clothes, not to be suspected, pleasant to look at, advanced in age, skilled in delivery, bold, with cut nails, should attend upon the sūtikā (woman in labour) with comforting, pleasant and truthful words, her lying on a soft bed on the ground covered with a very red bull's hide, face upward, with bent thighs and back.

text_flags.why: possible: 'prajanakaśalāḥ' is not a word; 'prajanana-kuśalāḥ' (skilled in delivery) fits; syllables na and ku lost.

notes: 'ābhugnasakthipṛṣṭhām' (with bent thighs and back) is taken as printed; the exact posture is not further described and the text may intend 'bent thighs' with a different word for the back. 'suraktārṣabhacarma' = well-red (or very red) hide of a bull. 'sūtikā' = a woman in childbirth / newly delivered; here in labour by context. 'ahatavāsasaḥ' = with new (unworn) cloth. The women are described by a series of adjectives; 'aśaṅkanīyāḥ' = not to be suspected (trustworthy).
